notes: Focused fix mirroring the reference: it collects placeholder names and a dynamic flag at provision time and classifies them in reverseproxy, with thorough tests covering end-to-end classification, direct ph() header reads, escaped literals, similar names and non-expression matchers; the only minor nit is that it returns the internal slice without cloning.

The retry fix is sound and matches the reference design (generic PlaceholderNames plus a reverseproxy-side classifier with good unit, handler and integration tests), but it also adds an unrelated behavioral change to IdleTimeoutWriter (DetachAfterHijack) along with its own test, which is serious scope creep.
Makes no changes, so the bug where request-only expressions retry successful responses remains.

Correctly classifies expressions at provision time from the type-checked AST, covering shorthand, direct ph() calls, escaped literals, similar-looking names and dynamic names, but it puts reverse-proxy-specific placeholder knowledge into the generic caddyhttp CEL matcher, which is a layering smell compared to exposing placeholder names and letting reverseproxy decide.
Identical to the reference fix, with the same comprehensive (if internals-coupled) test suite as C2/C4.

The master-socket redesign looks logically sound: it closes the dup'd fd, ref-counts under the lock and skips '@' names. But it rewrites unixSockets, the unixListener/unixConn fields and deleteListener (now pointer types), which is far more than the fix needed. Those type changes broke the package build against the PR tests (0/7, suite failed).
Identical to the reference fix, with thorough tests for refcounting, double close, close/relisten races, unixgram and abstract sockets.

Fixes the root cause (closes the dup'd fd, unlinks the stored addr under the lock, CAS double-close guard). It still runs the pre-bind unlink in reuseUnixSocket for '@' abstract names, so listening can delete a same-named file. Its abstract test builds a fake listener and so masks that gap.

Matches the reference: closes the dup'd file in reuse and does the decrement, close and unlink under the lock using Addr().String(). It adds a CAS guard against double Close and skips abstract names on both listen and close. Tests are broad, though somewhat coupled to internals.
Correct and consistent, but the zip symlink seek-past-end handling is ad hoc special-casing; tests cover copy and escape.
Production code matches the reference exactly, plus a sensible docs section and escape/squashfs tests; the zip unit test does not check seek or range.
Works, but it reads every zip symlink target eagerly at mount (costly on remote storage), adds shared helpers, and loosely accepts bare symlink names as roots.
Reference-equivalent behaviour with a tidy objectFromEntry helper, good tests including escape scenarios, and docs; the zip symlink check does not exclude directories.
Correct, with List and NewObject agreeing and root-at-symlink support, plus thorough tests; renaming the field causes needless struct realignment churn.
A clean exposedName helper keeps List and NewObject consistent, and the zip side mirrors the reference; tests and docs are solid.
Correct and consistent across zip and squashfs, keeps directories whose only members are skipped links, and has a very thorough test matrix; the unchecked StatT type assertion is a small smell.
Essentially the reference approach, cleanly done, with focused zip and squashfs unit tests; it has no copy or escape test.
Squashfs Open strips the `.rclonelink` suffix for regular files, so they open the wrong path; zip root matching also misses suffixed names.
Correct, but the root-alias logic is convoluted, the zip Open EOF behaviour change is tangential, and an existing test comment was edited.
Correct implementation with root handling and good tests, but it deletes an unrelated existing test comment.
Thorough and correct with an excellent cross-backend test matrix; the tangential zip Open EOF change and root dt tweak add slight scope creep.
Hides members beneath symlinks and adds a per-lookup path walk in squashfs, changing listing semantics beyond the spec; it also rewrites the escape log message.

Stores ctx in the Fs struct, merges symlink skips into the escape-name counter and rewrites that log message, uses a hacky Open condition, and has ordering bugs in newObjectNative; there are no squashfs tests and the new test is misplaced.
Hijacks the VFS Links option, and squashfs NewObject strips the suffix unconditionally so regular `.rclonelink` files break; Open treats any suffixed name as a link, and the tests are sloppy.

Works for listing, lookup and copy, but the zip side adds the suffix after root matching, so a root naming `link.txt.rclonelink` fails in zip while squashfs accepts it; it also stores a skip counter on the Fs struct.
Over-engineered (archiver helpers, deferred pending links, zipHasRoot), and squashfs NewObject still finds a symlink by its bare name without --links, so it disagrees with List.
Invents an unrequested 'safe target' policy that drops legitimate `..` and absolute links and even hides regular `.rclonelink` files, contradicting the spec.
